producer_report.summary:
I wrote docs/design/warm-baseline-build.md and added a CHANGELOG entry. The note says a local warm baseline would not shorten the checks stage for most jobs, and recommends extending CI-result reuse and warming the CI cache instead. Its supporting numbers come from my hand count and from estimates, labeled as such in the note.

It opens with how checks get results today. A CI result is requested first and polled up to ci_wait_s (1500 s); local checks run only as a fallback. It cites routing.rs and ci-routing.md section 4.1.

The Problem section splits the 14.1-minute checks stage by path. About 85% of jobs reuse a CI result and about 15% run locally. The one measured local run took about 19.3 minutes; the CI wait is largely an estimate.

The note corrects the freshness claim. Stable Cargo uses mtimes, so a fresh snapshot rebuilds every workspace crate and only third-party dependencies are reused. That lowers the per-run saving from 8.0 to about 4 minutes, and scaled to the local share it comes to about 0.6 minutes per landed job (estimate).

The note lists six alternatives, including warming the CI cache, extending CI-result reuse, a shared target directory, sccache and no change. It still cites review 20261029-155931-wfkr and says how the next review measures the saving.

checks_run.note: The scan reads tracked files only, so it did not see the new note. I reread the note against the banned words by eye.

criteria_check.criterion: The design has an Existing code section that reuses or extends crates/athena-core/src/routing.rs and docs/design/ci-routing.md, describing how checks get results today: CI result requested first, polled up to ci_wait_s, local checks only as fallback.
criteria_check.evidence: Section 1 of the note cites routing.rs (lines 10 to 20), athena.toml ci_wait_s = 1500, and ci-routing.md section 4.1 and section 10 item 3. I read all three before writing.

criteria_check.criterion: The Problem section gives measured durations for the CI-reuse path and the local-run path from recorded jobs (ci_result source and duration) or THROUGHPUT.md, with the source of each number and any unmeasured number labeled an estimate, and states what share of jobs run checks locally.
criteria_check.evidence: Section 2 has a per-path table. Local run: job 20261101-061448-sdya verification.json (fmt 2.4 s, clippy 34.6 s, test 1119.4 s, about 19.3 min), one sample. CI reuse: 463 s for one CI run, taken from the earlier verifier finding; the total wait is labeled an estimate. Local share is about 15 percent (9 of 61 verification records in 2026-11), counted by hand from the evidence snapshot. The ci_result record and THROUGHPUT.md are not present in the snapshot, and the note says so.

criteria_check.criterion: The 'Why this removes the bottleneck' section is derived from those per-path numbers, scales the 8.0-minute predicted saving to the local-fallback share, and says plainly if most jobs would not benefit, with a recommendation.
criteria_check.evidence: Section 4 scales 8.0 x 0.15 = 1.2 minutes, then about 0.6 minutes once mtime freshness is allowed for, with estimates labeled. It says most jobs would not benefit and recommends extending CI-result reuse and warming the CI cache instead.

criteria_check.criterion: Alternatives considered include extending or warming the CI-result path and CI target cache, with a reasoned comparison against the local warm baseline, alongside shared target dir, sccache and no change.
criteria_check.evidence: Section 5 lists six alternatives: no change, warm the CI path and cache, extend CI-result reuse, the local warm baseline, a shared target dir, and sccache.

criteria_check.criterion: The note corrects the freshness claim: stable Cargo uses file mtimes, a fresh snapshot rebuilds all workspace crates, only third-party deps are reused, and the estimate allows for it.
criteria_check.evidence: The 'Freshness' subsection of section 3 states the mtime rule and that all workspace crates rebuild. Section 4 lowers the per-run saving from 8.0 to about 4 minutes because only third-party dependencies are reused.

criteria_check.criterion: The note still cites review 20261029-155931-wfkr and states how the next throughput review measures the saving (median minutes per landed job over the last 20, checks stage vs 14.1 and 25.4, split by CI vs local).
criteria_check.evidence: The opening paragraph, section 2 and section 7 cite the review. Section 7 gives the median minutes per landed job over the last 20 landings, the checks stage against 14.1 and the total against 25.4, split by CI versus local.

criteria_check.criterion: git diff shows changes only to docs/design/warm-baseline-build.md and CHANGELOG.md; rust-toolchain.toml, athena.toml, defaults.toml, Cargo.lock, crates/ and .github/workflows/ are unchanged.
criteria_check.evidence: I edited only the note (new file) and CHANGELOG.md. The build created no tracked changes, because the target directory is outside the working copy.

open_issues: The next throughput review should replace the hand-counted shares and the single local sample with medians from the ci_result records.
mistakes: The 85/15 split is a hand count of verification.json files, not the ci_result record. A job whose verification.json lacks the reuse note might have run its checks locally for a reason I did not check, or have no checks at all.
The 4-minute per-local-run saving rests on an unmeasured guess that third-party compile is about half of a cold build. The note labels it an estimate.
The CI-wait figure (8 to 15 minutes) is an estimate. The only measured number is one 463 s CI test run, taken from the earlier verifier finding.
learnings: The first attempt's note was not in this copy, so I wrote the note from scratch. The working copy has no THROUGHPUT.md.
Reused CI checks show duration 0.0 s with basis 'recorded result' and reused: true in verification.json.
About 52 of the 61 verification records in 2026-11 contain 'result reused from the CI run'.
The policy scan reads only tracked files, so it does not scan a newly created file.
desires: THROUGHPUT.md and the ci_result records (source and duration per job) in the snapshot, so the per-path split could be measured instead of hand-counted.
A recorded CI-wait duration for reused checks. The reused check's own duration is 0.0 s, so the wait is not visible in verification.json.
